title: 10 Best Cafes in Chumphon Town 2026 — Chill, Photo, Coffee
metaDesc: The best cafes in Chumphon town, Thailand for all-day lounging, photos and good coffee — from the old-house Comienzo House to seaside Rolly Cafe, with areas, prices and real opening hours.

ogTitle: Best Cafes in Chumphon Town — 10 Spots to Chill, Shoot, Sip
ogDesc: Comfortable, photogenic cafes in Chumphon town with good coffee, plus areas, prices and real opening hours.
intro: Chumphon is the robusta capital of Thailand, so it's no surprise the town has plenty of cafes and most of the coffee is solid. From renovated old-house cafes where you can work in quiet to seaside slow bars roasting their own beans, we rounded up spots that sit in town or a short drive away — comfy to linger in, easy to photograph — and we'll tell you straight what each one is actually good at.

blocks.html: A lot of people only stop in Chumphon to catch the boat to Koh Tao or Koh Samui, and miss the town's cafes entirely. This is where Thailand grows the most robusta, so most cafes pour local beans at prices lighter than big-city spots. A black coffee or latte still runs around ฿50–90, and quite a few places roast their own beans too.

We picked places that are genuinely comfortable to sit in, have a good photo corner, and don't coast on name alone. They're ordered from the easiest-to-reach spots in town, working outward toward the seaside and edge-of-town cafes that take a bit more driving but earn it on the view.
Prices are rough ranges and may shift with the menu and time of day. Some places close on certain weekdays, so checking the shop's page before you head out is the safer bet.

items.name: Comienzo House
items.blurb: A cafe renovated from an old house in the Na Thung area of Chumphon town. The two-storey building is split into several seating nooks, each warmly decorated like sitting in a friend's home, and you can shoot photos at nearly any spot. Quiet enough to open a laptop and work for hours. The house-made cakes are the thing people order again.
items.meta: Uthumphon Rd, Na Thung, Mueang · Open 9.00–18.00

items.name: Baan Kao Cafe (Das alte Kaffeehaus)
items.blurb: An old wooden-house cafe in the Bang Mak area that locals rate as the town's standout cake spot. The mood is classic and warm, with a rotating lineup of homemade cakes. Coffee is decent, but this is more a place to sit over a sweet in the afternoon than to settle in and work.
items.meta: Bang Mak, Mueang · Homemade cake shop

items.name: Morning Drug Cafe
items.blurb: A clean-lined, white-toned minimalist cafe wrapped in greenery, with both indoor and outdoor zones plus a co-working corner for getting things done. The house-made croissants are what people talk about, and drinks come with an oat-milk option for anyone who skips dairy.

items.name: The Glass Cafe & Restaurant
items.blurb: A two-storey, white-toned glass cafe in town — bright and open, with plenty of check-in corners. It runs as both a restaurant and a cafe, so you can sit down for a full meal and carry on with coffee. There's an air-conditioned zone and a garden zone, parking is easy, and it suits groups or families.

items.name: BEEN BARISTORY
items.blurb: A specialty cafe in town blending loft and vintage looks in an easy, sea-toned palette. It's strong on matcha — strawberry matcha and yuzu matcha — alongside hand-picked coffee and cocoa. There are beach-chair corners and window-side seats that photograph well.

items.name: Rolly Cafe (Coffee and Roaster)
items.blurb: A seaside slow bar in the Pak Nam area of Chumphon, done up surf-club style. The warm timber space has several seafront photo corners, and they roast their own beans for a rounded, not-too-intense cup. Fresh sweets like cheese pie and brownie pair well with the coffee. It's small with limited parking, and closed on Tuesdays.
items.meta: Pak Nam, Mueang · Open 10.00–17.00, closed Tue

items.name: Home Coffee
items.blurb: A shophouse cafe in the Sukhaphiban area of town, split into a coffee zone up front and a seating zone in back. The retro styling is easy to sit in, prices are friendly, and it suits a morning cup or a rest break between walks around town. Nothing flashy, but it does the basics well.

items.name: Montong Cafe
items.blurb: A retro-styled shipping-container cafe near Phetkasem Road on the Ao Urai market side. It's split into a coffee-and-bakery zone and a steak zone, which suits drivers passing through who want coffee and a snack in one stop. The container corners make for cute photos.
items.meta: Near Phetkasem, Ao Urai market · Shipping container

items.name: 48 House Restaurant & Cafe
items.blurb: A stylishly done cafe-restaurant with lots of space, out near the entrance to Wat Khu Khut on the edge of Chumphon town. The menu spans Thai and Western dishes, so it works for settling in over a main meal then carrying on with coffee. The open layout lets kids run around, making it more of a family spot than a solo-work one.
items.meta: Wat Khu Khut entrance, edge of town · Cafe + food

items.name: Me Bakery & Coffee Shop
items.blurb: A bakery cafe out by Thung Wua Laen Beach, near Cabana Beach, strong on desserts and house-baked goods. It suits anyone heading to the Thung Wua Laen sea who wants a spot to rest, sip coffee and grab a sweet. It's not in town, but it's a short drive from the center.
items.meta: Near Thung Wua Laen Beach · Bakery cafe

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Not every spot on this list is a serious coffee place — some shine more for cake or atmosphere than for the bean itself. If you're coming specifically for self-roasted local coffee, focus on Rolly Cafe and BEEN BARISTORY. If you want to settle in and work in quiet, Comienzo House and Morning Drug Cafe do the job better.

blocks.text: Pick a cafe by the vibe you want

blocks.html: Each cafe in Chumphon town is good at something different. Grouping them like this makes the choice easier.

items.name: For working
items.blurb: Want plugs, Wi-Fi and quiet seats? Try Comienzo House or Morning Drug Cafe, which has a co-working corner.

items.name: For photos
items.blurb: After pretty shots for the feed? Go for seaside Rolly Cafe, or Baan Kao Cafe with its classic mood.

items.name: For serious coffee
items.blurb: Want to taste self-roasted local robusta? Head to Rolly Cafe and BEEN BARISTORY, both focused on the bean and the brew.

items.name: With family
items.blurb: Want space and proper meals? Try The Glass Cafe or 48 House, where kids can run around.

blocks.text: Why Chumphon coffee is worth a try

blocks.html: Chumphon has grown the most robusta in Thailand for decades. Lately a new generation of farmers has raised the bar on processing — drying, fermenting, sorting the beans — so the local robusta isn't just the dark, bitter cup people once assumed, but carries roasted-nut and chocolate notes that coffee fans enjoy. Many cafes in town have an edge here: a local bean that's hard to find elsewhere.

items: Lighter prices than big cities — black coffee or latte mostly runs ฿50–90, cheaper than cafes in Bangkok or Chiang Mai
Local beans, self-roasted — plenty of places use Chumphon robusta roasted on-site, for a flavor that's genuinely of the place
Souvenirs on the spot — cafes that roast their own usually sell beans and drip bags to take home
Not yet crowded — Chumphon's cafes aren't as packed as the big tourist towns, so you can sit easy without fighting for a table

blocks.text: A cafe-hopping trip in Chumphon town

blocks.html: If you have a half-day to a full day in Chumphon town, here's a cafe route that loops through town in the morning and closes out by the sea in the evening, without driving all over the place.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Cafes in town + a seaside finish

items.activity: Start the morning at Comienzo House
items.note: First cup with cake, grab a quiet corner, shoot the old house before it gets busy

items.activity: Move on to Morning Drug Cafe
items.note: Try the house-made croissant; if you need to open a laptop, there's a co-working corner
Try bold southern Thai food or a rice-and-curry plate before the afternoon cup
Try the matcha or a hand-picked coffee, and grab the window-side photo corner

items.activity: Finish at seaside Rolly Cafe in Pak Nam
items.note: Sit in the sea breeze, sip self-roasted coffee with cheese pie — check first that it's not Tuesday, when it's closed

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Out to the edge of town + the sea

items.activity: Start at The Glass Cafe for a long breakfast
items.note: A bright glass cafe with proper meals — good for an unhurried start to the day

items.activity: Stop by Montong Cafe near Phetkasem
items.note: Shoot the shipping-container corner and try a snack on the way through

items.activity: Drive to Thung Wua Laen Beach
items.note: Swim or walk the beach in the afternoon

items.activity: Rest at Me Bakery & Coffee near Cabana Beach
items.note: Sip coffee with house-baked goods, and close the day on the Thung Wua Laen sea view

faq.q: Which cafes in Chumphon town are good for working?
faq.a: Comienzo House in Na Thung is quiet with several long-stay corners, while Morning Drug Cafe has a co-working corner and Wi-Fi — both are good for opening a laptop. It's worth avoiding busy weekend afternoons.

faq.q: Which Chumphon cafe is the most photogenic?
faq.a: If you like seaside corners, Rolly Cafe in the Pak Nam area is done up surf-club style with plenty of photo spots. For a classic, warm mood, Baan Kao Cafe and Comienzo House shoot well from every angle.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost in Chumphon cafes?
faq.a: Most black coffees or lattes run around ฿50–90 depending on the shop and menu — lighter than big-city cafes — and many places use local robusta roasted on-site.

faq.q: Which cafes in Chumphon town roast their own beans?
faq.a: Rolly Cafe in Pak Nam roasts its own beans and has an in-house roastery, while BEEN BARISTORY is a specialty cafe focused on hand-picked coffee. Both suit anyone coming specifically to drink serious coffee.

faq.q: Do you need your own car to do the Chumphon cafe scene?
faq.a: In town, many cafes are close enough to walk between or reach by motorbike taxi. But for the seaside spots like Rolly Cafe or Me Bakery out near Thung Wua Laen, having your own car is far more convenient.
